citation: Thompson, James. Plat of the Town of Chicago. Illinois and Michigan Canal Commissioners, completed 4 August 1830.
author: James Thompson
repository: Chicago History Museum (working copy, ICHi-34284); the original burned in the 1871 fire
locator: chicago/pre_fire_v1/maps/images/1830_thompson_plat.png (the sheet held in this repository; read for its stated figures, never traced for geometry)
note: PARAMETER SOURCE, not a warping raster — no open high-resolution archival scan located, and the surviving artifact is a Canal Commissioners' working copy dated to at least 1836. Its value is the hard dimensional module: the original Town of Chicago at roughly 0.375 sq mi, 80-ft streets, 18-ft alleys. Generate street and alley geometry analytically from those figures rather than tracing pixels. A COPY OF THE SHEET IS HELD IN THIS REPOSITORY at chicago/pre_fire_v1/maps/images/1830_thompson_plat.png — the owner pointed T-0444 at it on 2026-09-03 for the West Division's lot dimensions and block lot-counts, which are READ off it as figures; the rule above still governs geometry. `verified` flips to true in the commit that reads it. READ FOR ITS WATERCOURSES on 2026-09-04 under T-0452, at 5x on the repository copy: the sheet draws ONE watercourse and only one — two freehand banks running north out of the main stem across North Division block 6, crossing the block's alley and North Water Street and flaring at the mouth — and draws none anywhere else in the North, West or South Divisions. It is therefore NOT the source of the "three sloughs off the Main Branch" count, which is Conley/Stelzer 1933's; see docs/RESEARCH/thompson_plat_sloughs.md. The reading is of what is drawn and where, by block and lot; no course is traced from it, the rule above still governing geometry.
